reviews.summary: Re-scored against the CONFIRMED v1 target (1-2 tenants, Workers Paid, Clerk, MONTHLY_COST_CEILING_USD=400, scale-out deferred to Phase N), not a hypothetical hyperscale deployment. On the Cloudflare-primitive-correctness lens the document is now strong and, importantly, RIGHT-SIZED: the four deployment facts are integrated consistently across §1.1a/§1.2/§2.7/§5.1/§10.1/§10.3 and the Appendix "Confirmed decisions" block, with no residual "IdP TBD" or "unknown scale" placeholders. Every load-bearing CF claim I could check verifies against primary docs (2026-06): (1) Workers AI Neuron pricing $0.011/1k Neurons + 10,000 Neurons/day included on Paid — exact; (2) AI Gateway spend limits apply only to Unified-Billing/BYOK rails "for models with known pricing," so the all-@cf/ binding-based v1 set is NOT gateway-enforceable and the app-level token_spend 429 pre-check correctly IS the enforcing cap (the contentious cross-round "debris" point survives docs verification); (3) Vectorize 10M vectors/index (Jan-2026 increase) + topK ceiling 100, dropping to 50 only with returnValues/returnMetadata:'all' — the §5.3.2 vector arm correctly returns only {id,score} to keep the full 100 budget, uses the $in metadata operator for multi-scope grants, respects the 64-byte metadata-indexability caveat, and frames the namespace as a query-time partition (NOT a security boundary) with the D1 re-check as the authoritative gate. The right-sizing is explicit and correct: single D1, sharding deferred, tenant_shards columns resolve to one shard, Vectorize/D1 ceilings labeled NON-BINDING and reframed as Phase-N triggers; the §10.7 single-writer-D1 write-throughput axis and ctx.waitUntil-decoupled recall traces are the correct CF idiom. Workers AI per-model rate limits are explicitly labeled conservative ASSUMPTIONS, unverified-until-staging, non-binding at 1-2 tenants, degrade-or-queue (never 429 the user) — the correct posture; AI Gateway + BYO/OpenAI-compatible upgrade path is documented behind the embed()/gen()/rerank() chokepoints and not built in v1. No critical or high issue remains; the score cap-below-60 rule (unresolved critical) does not apply. Residual debris is minor: one MEDIUM spec gap (where token_spend.neurons is written — app-computed post-call vs lagged gateway log — is never specified, which is the hard-cap-vs-soft-cap distinction; non-binding at 1-2 tenants) and two LOW items (the rate-limit assumption numbers conflict across three sections; the hard daily 10k-Neuron Workers AI allotment is distinct from the monthly USD ceiling the enforcer keys on). These are the "clear the round-7 debris" cleanups, not design defects.

reviews.summary: Requirements-coverage / internal-consistency re-score after integrating the four confirmed deployment facts (1-2 tenants v1 / Workers Paid / Clerk / $400 configurable ceiling) with scale-out deferred to Phase-N. The four facts are genuinely and consistently integrated — no surviving contradictions of the now-decided values. (1) The 1-2-tenant target is stated authoritatively in §1.1a and threaded through G8, Non-Goals, SC9, §2, §3.1.4, §5.1, §10.5/§10.7, and the appendix; every "unknown" that remains is the explicitly-bounded "vector/session counts unknown but SMALL," not an "unknown scale" hedge. (2) Scale-out deferral is consistent at every sharding mention: §1.1a, G8, Non-Goals, the §2 ASCII, the tenant_shards DDL (§3.1.4 carries an explicit "SINGLE-SHARD in v1, db_binding='DB'" comment), §3.2, ScopedDB/ScopedVectorize (§7.3 resolve to 'DB'/'brain-chunks'), §10.1 wrangler config, and the §10.7 Phase-N triggers — nowhere is sharding treated as v1 build work. (3) Clerk is confirmed everywhere with explicit "not IdP TBD" language (§1.1a, §7.2 line 2725, §10.3 line 4220, appendix #7). (4) The $400 ceiling (configurable, per-tenant-overridable) is consistent across SC8, §1.1a, §2, §5.1/§5f, §9.1.3, §10.1 vars, and appendix #8. Rate-limit hedges are uniformly relabeled as "assumed, conservative, non-binding at 1-2 tenants" rather than "pending." The appendix consolidates all 8 confirmed decisions as a single source of truth and marks each carried-forward open question RESOLVED or as a v1-irrelevant tuning task. Residual defects are minor and do not touch the four facts: (a) a real internal-consistency nick — the §10.1 "Plan, models & rate limits" block states embed ~300 req/min (§5.1/appendix say ~3000 — a 10x contradiction) and synthesis ~100 req/min (§5.1/appendix say ~300), while line 4181 claims that very block is "configured against" the §5.1 values, so §10.1 asserts fidelity to §5.1 while contradicting it twice; this is one stale block, non-binding operationally but a direct numeric self-contradiction; (b) line 1573's Workflow-id retention caveat still cites "3 days Free / 30 days Paid" as if the plan were undecided — now that Paid is confirmed the operative window is unambiguously 30 days and the Free branch is non-applicable residue; (c) "iter-N"/"iteration-N" revision-provenance tags remain pervasive (dozens) — not contradictions, but cosmetic debris for a finished PRD. On the "R7 debris": I could verify no surviving unknown-scale / IdP-TBD / rate-pending hedges and that the deferral/fact integration is clean, but the specific round-7 review item-list is an external artifact not contained in the PRD, so I cannot positively cross-check each R7 item was cleared by name — I report only what the document itself substantiates. Net: a large improvement on the lens; the four facts are well-integrated with no critical contradiction (nothing caps below 60). Fix the §10.1 rate-limit numbers and the line-1573 Free-plan residue.

strengths: Single structural choke-point (ScopedDB/ScopedVectorize/ScopedR2) with an ESLint banned-import rule converts isolation from convention to a compile-time-enforced control; no read arm (FTS, vector, graph, facts) can bind tenant_id while skipping the scope/visibility gate, and there is explicitly no raw-SQL passthrough.

Write side actually populates the columns the read predicates depend on: §8.3 stamps session visibility/user_id/team_id onto transcript chunks, chunks.visibility is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'world' CHECK-constrained, and writeFact forces user_id=p.userId + role-constrains visibility — so canary #8's intra-tenant private-session leak is backed by a real data model, not just a read-side assertion.

trust_grade is provably nowhere in the vector path — authoritative ChunkMeta enumerated without it, not a metadata index, foldPartitionFilter folds only scope, boost runs post-hydration on the sidecar — so a trust promotion never re-upserts a vector and never participates in partitioning.

Recall-cliff fix (foldPartitionFilter {scope:{$in:[...]}}) correctly keeps the restricted-principal topK=100 budget inside the grant via ONE query, while keeping visibility authoritative at D1 (declining the pushdown that would drop the principal's own private chunks) — a subtle, correct call.

Break-glass is a textbook fail-closed audited carve-out: org-role-gated, 403 for non-admins incl. forged breakGlass:true, in-batch audit row + guaranteed alert, intra-tenant only, with canaries #14/#15 asserting both the deny and the audited-success paths.
API-key mint pins allowed_scopes=intersect(request, minter.allowedScopes), closing the one-step privilege-escalation path a restricted Persona-C member could otherwise use to mint a tenant-wide key.

Table-driven canary meta-test treats visibility as a third isolation axis spanning facts AND chunks AND graph, so a new read surface that bypasses readFacts/visibilityPredicate/the typed frontier methods fails CI — isolation coverage scales with the surface.

weaknesses.issue: Four Code-reference annotation lines (≈554, 1619, 2098, 3381) still describe Vectorize metadata as including trust_grade ('move team_id/scope/trust_grade/embedding_model to metadata', 'scope/type/trust_grade as metadata filters'), directly contradicting the authoritative §3.2/§4.9 design which states trust_grade is deliberately NOT a Vectorize field. This is stale round-debris, not an actual leak (the load-bearing ChunkMeta and foldPartitionFilter are clean), but it is exactly the kind of contradiction that misleads an implementer porting from the cited source.
weaknesses.recommendation: Edit the four code-reference lines to read 'move team_id/scope/visibility/embedding_model to metadata; trust_grade stays in the memory_use_policy sidecar (never a Vectorize field)' so the annotations match the authoritative §3.2 shape.

weaknesses.issue: The FTS arm's inline SQL (§5.3.1, lines 1761-1769) filters tenant_id + scope but does NOT apply the visibility predicate inline; visibility is only enforced when the returned ids are hydrated through getChunksByIds. This is correct per the 'D1 re-check is authoritative' model and the end-to-end result is gated, but a reader could mistake the inline arm as fully self-gating and a future refactor that consumes FTS ids without the mandatory hydration step would leak private-session chunk existence on the keyword arm.
weaknesses.recommendation: Add one sentence to §5.3.1 making explicit that the FTS arm's inline predicate is tenant+scope only and that the visibility tier is enforced at the mandatory getChunksByIds hydration (never bypass hydration for FTS ids) — mirroring the note already present for the vector arm.

weaknesses.issue: visibilityPredicate's team branch evaluates to sql`0` when p.teamIds is empty, and resolves team rows via team_id IN (p.teamIds). This is correct, but the security guarantee depends entirely on principalFromMembership populating teamIds completely from ALL of the user's membership rows in the active tenant. A user with multiple membership rows (one per team) relies on highestRole + the teamIds flatMap being exhaustive; there is no canary explicitly asserting that a user who is a member of teams T1 and T2 (two rows) gets BOTH in teamIds (only the single-team recall case #9 is specified).
weaknesses.recommendation: Add a canary (or extend #9) asserting that a user with multiple team-membership rows in one tenant recalls team rows for ALL their teams (teamIds is the union across membership rows), guarding against a regression where principalFromMembership collapses to a single row.

reviews.summary: Against the CONFIRMED v1 target (1-2 tenants, Workers Paid, Clerk, $400/mo configurable, scale-out deferred to Phase-N), the multi-tenant + intra-tenant isolation story is sound and no critical leak survives. All seven lens checks pass on both the read AND write sides. (1) §9.0.1/§7.2 membership resolution is tenant-bound: the lookup is WHERE user_id=? AND tenant_id=?, the active tenant is pinned per-surface and re-checked against memberships, and an unspecified tenant errors 401 (never a silent first-membership default) — a multi-tenant user is bound to exactly one tenant per request. (2) foldPartitionFilter collapses any number of granted scopes to a single {scope:{$in:[...]}} query, derived from the principal's own grant, and ScopedVectorize.query independently re-authorizes any explicit scope filter against allowedScopes, so no ungranted scope leaks; visibility is deliberately NOT pushed (correct — it would drop the principal's own private chunks). (3) The link-arm getLinks/expandFrontier are typed ScopedDB methods that apply nodeGate (scope AND visibility) to BOTH endpoints (nf/nt) with no raw-SQL escape hatch; the BFS, getLinks, and get_backlinks gate identically, and the seed is resolved through nodeVisible/resolveScopedNode before the walk. (4) trust_grade is genuinely absent from the entire vector path: the authoritative ChunkMeta upsert blob (§3.2/§4.9) enumerates exactly {documentId,teamId,scope,visibility,userId,embeddingModel,chunkIndex,path,tenant_id} with no trustGrade, it is not a metadata index, foldPartitionFilter folds only scope, and the trust boost runs post-hydration on the LEFT-JOINed sidecar. (5) Break-glass remains fail-closed (403 for non-admins, including a forged breakGlass:true), org-role-gated, writes a breakglass_read audit row in-batch, fires a high-severity alert every call, is intra-tenant only (never bypasses tenant_id), and is covered by canaries #14/#15. (6) Isolation is intact despite single-D1: ScopedDB injects tenant_id + scopePredicate + visibilityPredicate at one choke-point with an ESLint banned-import control, ScopedVectorize hard-wires namespace=tenantId with a D1 re-check as the correctness gate, and the §3.1.8 coverage matrix confirms chunks/facts/pages carry tenant_id+visibility+user_id+team_id (entities the {world,team} subset). Crucially the WRITE side backs the read predicates: §8.3 stamps the session's visibility/user_id/team_id onto transcript chunks (overriding the 'world' default that correctly applies only to org-knowledge ingested docs), chunks.visibility is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'world' CHECK-constrained, writeFact forces user_id=p.userId and constrains visibility by role, and §7.1 mint pins allowed_scopes=intersect(request, minter.allowedScopes) so a restricted member cannot one-step-escalate to tenant-wide. The only residue is non-load-bearing documentation debris: four Code-reference annotation lines still say 'trust_grade as metadata filter,' contradicting the (correct) authoritative body. Tag and fix; it does not cap the score.
